$comment: D-TARGET-ARM64-FP16-CONVERSION-FORMS-UNDECLARED (P55, lane fp) — the four half-precision `fcvt` forms, witnessed by EXECUTION. ★★★ WHY RUNNING IT MATTERS WHEN THE GAP FAILED LOUD: the refusal was loud, so a build-only arm goes green the moment any opcode exists — but the six `fcvt` forms differ only in `type` [23:22] and `opc` [16:15], so a wrong field makes `fcvt h0, d1` read a double's low 32 bits as a float, or `fcvt s0, h1` write a double-shaped pattern into a register the caller reads as a float. Both compile rc=0 and both give wrong numbers. ★★★ THE DISCRIMINATOR IS PRECISION LOSS: binary16 keeps 10 explicit mantissa bits, so 1/3 becomes exactly 0.333251953125 and can never become itself again. Shapes 1-6 assert that number across all four forms PAIRWISE (each form appears in two shapes with a different partner, so one wrong word reddens two shapes that share nothing else) and shapes 2 and 4 assert the round trip DISAGREES with its input, so nothing here can pass over a template that emitted nothing. ★★ SATURATION AND UNDERFLOW ARE THE SECOND DISCRIMINATOR — binary16's largest finite value is 65504, so 1e30 becomes +inf and 1e-30 becomes +0 (shapes 8-10, 13), answers no wider format gives for those inputs — and shapes 11-12 convert 65504 itself and get it back EXACTLY, which is what stops the saturation shapes from being satisfied by an instruction that always saturates. ⚠⚠ NOT ONE SHAPE IS A COPY: ✔MEASURED in P54, an inline-asm `fmov %d0, %d1` reaches the binary as ZERO INSTRUCTIONS because copy coalescing plus `classifyIdentityClassMove` deletes it; every template here changes the value's WIDTH and its BITS, twice. ⚠ FP16 ARITHMETIC IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT — ✔MEASURED, gas 2.42 and clang 18.1.3 both refuse `fadd h0,h1,h2`, `fmov h0,h1` and the fp16 INTEGER conversions `fcvtzs w0,h1` / `scvtf h0,w1` at the default -march; only FCVT has half arms in base ARMv8-A, so writing any of the others would be ABOVE the union. ⚠ `volatile` seeds are load-bearing: the release arm must still reach the templates. ⚠ ARM64 SPECS ONLY — the subject is one target's encodings for one mnemonic. Exit codes name the failing shape.
